thread.title: Nasdaq Outpaces Dow Jones, Gas Prices Lift S&P 500 | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Nasdaq Outpaces Dow Jones, Gas Prices Lift S&P 500 | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Dow Jones industrial average, the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 all jumped at Wednesday open, but quickly backed away from their opening highs. Premarket trade turned sharply higher on positive consumer price data. Earnings news and natural gas and oil prices were early factors in today's stock market . Progress in Britain's Brexit negotiations with the European Union also influenced early action.
X FANG stocks stepped firmly higher, driving the Nasdaq — Amazon.com ( AMZN ) jumped 2%; Facebook ( FB ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) each rose more than 1%. Apple ( AAPL ) reversed early gains and dropped 0.5% following an analyst downgrade . Earnings news was mixed, with marijuana stocks off to a disappointing open as Tilray ( TLRY ) and Canopy Growth ( CGC ) fell after their earnings reports. Canada Goose ( GOOS ), Qiwi ( QIWI ) and chipmaker Macom Technology Solutions ( MTSI ) all chalked up strong earnings-related moves.
The Nasdaq was up 0.8% and off early highs. The Dow Jones industrial average climbed 0.6% and the S&P 500 notched a 0.7% gain.
Among Dow Jones stocks, Nike ( NKE ) led the industrials, up nearly 3%. China's Ctrip.com International ( CTRP ) topped the Nasdaq 100.
Oil prices rose ahead of data due after the stock market open; natural gas prices spiked to a four-year high. The result spun natural gas stocks into mixed early trade and to the some of the S&P 500's top early gains: Chesapeake Energy ( CHK ) led the S&P 500, while Cabot Oil & Gas ( COG ) and Range Resources ( RRC ) quickly reversed into declines. Utility Pacific Gas & Electric ( PCG ), beset by uncertainty as to its responsibility in the northern California wildfire, posted the S&P 500's largest early decline.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Dow Jones Stock Apple At A Crossroads; Canada Goose Tops Buy Point Apple stock opened narrowly above its 200-day line, then slipped back below support as Guggenheim Securities downgraded the stock to neutral, from buy. The note also removed the stock's 245 price target, noting that periods of rapid iPhone price appreciation point to a period of consolidation in the device's pricing power. Apple shares have pulled back a bit less than 18% from an Oct. 3 high. The stock could begin to fashion a bottom to a potential base around the 200-day level. Signs of accumulation and for tight weekly closes would be bullish stock chart signals. A decisive break below 200-day support would signal the stock was in for a longer and possibly deeper consolidation.
Cannabis stock Tilray dumped almost 5% in early trading. The Canadian supplier reported a narrower-than-expected loss and an 86% jump in revenue late Tuesday. The volatile July initial public offering is consolidating, in its third week below its 10-week moving average and 63% below its September high.
Canopy Growth toppled more than 6% as losses deepened in its fiscal second quarter . Revenue jumped 33%, but sales and marketing expenses soared 413%, throttling any potential bottom line gains. The six-month-old stock is down 36% from its October high, and 25% above its May IPO price.
High-ticket outerwear maker Canada Goose knocked out a 21% opening gain. The company reported a surprise earnings gain of 46 cents per share , vs. views for a decline to 19 cents. Revenue jumped 34%. The move sent shares past a double-bottom base buy point at 65.92. The gap up open past a buy point, called a breakaway gap , sets up a buy range beginning at the stock's open price. In this case that would set the buy range between 66.84 and 70.18. Keep in mind that buying under the " uptrend under pressure " warning flag requires special caution.
Natural Gas Prices Soar, Chesapeake Leads S&P 500 Oil prices climbed, with West Texas Intermediate up 1.2% and back above $56 a barrel. Still, WTI is down nearly 7% for the week, its worst week since February. Now nearly 28% off its early October high, oil prices have undercut February lows to trade at their lowest level since December. A report from the International Energy Agency said rising U.S. oil production and increased supply from Russia and Saudi Arabia had more than compensated for oil taken off the global market by U.S. sanctions against Iran.
Weekly oil inventories data are due out at 10:30 a.m. ET from the U.S. Energy Information Administration.
Natural gas narrowed its early advance to 7% early Wednesday, to $4.39 per million British thermal units. Tight storage levels and forecasts for cold weather have driven prices up around 60% since mid-September. Prices snapped long-term resistance at the $4 level, moving to their highest mark since November 2014.
Among S&P 500 stocks,Chesapeake Energy surged 5% to lead the index. Cabot Oil & Gas and Range Resources both surged at the open, but quickly backtracked to trade about 1% lower apiece.
Inflation Eases, China Stock Markets Dip, Europe's Markets Strengthen Consumer price gains accelerated in October, rising 0.3% for the month, but growth of the core CPI inflation gauge slowed to 2.1%, year-over-year, the Labor Department said. Prices were in line with economist projections , but the slowing core CPI reading raised questions regarding the Federal Reserve's rate hike strategy.
China stock markets closed modestly lower. In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 bobbed 0.2% higher after Tuesday's steep decline. In Europe, London's FTSE 100 gained 0.2%, buoyed by progress in the U.K.'s Brexit negotiations with the European Union. The CAC-40 in Paris tightened its early loss to less than 0.1%. Frankfurt's DAX reversed its early losses and gained 0.2% in afternoon trade.
